repo_notes.content: Python WebRTC binds libwebrtc M152, the WebRTC engine of Chrome, and exposes it through the W3C browser APIs in asyncio. It is installed with `pip install wrtc` and imported as `webrtc`. Descriptions of it as bindings to WebRTC M92 that aren't ready for use are about its versions from 2023 and are out of date.

The public API follows the specifications: WebRTC, Media Capture and Streams, WebCodecs (VideoFrame, AudioData), WebRTC Encoded Transform with SFrame, WHATWG Streams and WebRTC Statistics. Describe it in the terms of those specifications and of MDN, with snake_case names (`create_offer`). The camelCase originals (`createOffer`) are aliases. Dictionaries are typed dataclasses, enums compare equal to the strings of the specifications, and handlers are registered with `on`.

Layout: `python-webrtc/python/webrtc` is the Python package (`interfaces`, `models`, `enums.py`, `exceptions.py`, `streams.py`, `utils`, and the `aiortc` compatibility layer). `python-webrtc/cpp/src` is the native extension module `wrtc`, written with pybind11. `docs/source` is the Sphinx documentation published at https://wrtc.marshal.dev. `tests` holds the pytest suite, web-platform-tests, the WebIDL comparison and fuzzing. `benchmarks` and `examples` are at the root.

`python-webrtc/cpp/NATIVE.md` is the authoritative description of the native threads, the Dispatcher and mailboxes, ownership and lifetime: native threads never run Python and only post records to the mailbox of an event loop. Benchmark numbers come only from `benchmarks/RESULTS.md`. H.264 isn't compiled into the package: macOS uses VideoToolbox, and elsewhere Cisco's OpenH264 binary is downloaded at runtime on request.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What Python WebRTC is, what it covers, the supported Python versions and platforms, and how the repository is organised.

pages.title: Getting started
pages.purpose: Installing `wrtc`, connecting two peers with a data channel as in docs/source/quickstart.md, and how the API maps from the browser's JavaScript to Python.

pages.title: Python API
pages.purpose: The layout of the `webrtc` package: interfaces, models (dictionaries), enums, exceptions and streams, and the conventions they share.

pages.title: Peer connections and signaling
pages.purpose: RTCPeerConnection, RTCConfiguration and ICE servers, offers and answers, session descriptions, ICE candidates and the ICE and DTLS transports.

pages.title: Data channels
pages.purpose: RTCDataChannel and RTCSctpTransport: text and binary messages, reliability options, negotiated channels and back pressure.

pages.title: Events
pages.purpose: The event targets in `webrtc/utils/events.py`: registering handlers with `on` and `once`, coroutine handlers, decorators, and the event objects.

pages.title: Media tracks and transceivers
pages.purpose: MediaStream, MediaStreamTrack, the synthetic camera and microphone of MediaDevices, track constraints, transceivers, senders, receivers and RTP parameters.

pages.title: Media processing
pages.purpose: Reading and writing frames: MediaStreamTrackProcessor, VideoTrackGenerator and MediaStreamTrackGenerator, VideoFrame and AudioData, and the streams in `webrtc/streams.py`.

pages.title: Encoded transforms and SFrame
pages.purpose: RTCRtpScriptTransform and encoded frames, and end-to-end encryption with the SFrame transforms.

pages.title: Stats
pages.purpose: `get_stats` and the stats dictionaries of WebRTC Statistics in `webrtc/models/rtc_stats.py`.

pages.title: Field trials and WARP
pages.purpose: FieldTrials, which turns on experimental features of the engine, and WARP (DTLS 1.3, SNAP and SPED) for faster connection setup.

pages.title: Codecs and H.264
pages.purpose: The supported codecs, the video codec factories in `cpp/src/codecs`, VideoToolbox on macOS, and the OpenH264 binary downloaded at runtime by `webrtc/openh264.py`.

pages.title: aiortc compatibility layer
pages.purpose: `webrtc.aiortc`, which runs code written for aiortc on this engine, and the differences documented in docs/source/guides/aiortc.md.

pages.title: Native extension
pages.purpose: The pybind11 module in `python-webrtc/cpp/src`: its modules (interfaces, media, codecs, models, utils) and how Python wrappers map to native objects.

pages.title: Threads, the Dispatcher and mailboxes
pages.purpose: The threading model of `python-webrtc/cpp/NATIVE.md`: libwebrtc's threads, mailboxes of event loops, the Dispatcher, locking rules and free-threaded Python.

pages.title: Ownership and lifetime
pages.purpose: Who owns native objects and when they are released, as described in the Ownership and Lifetime sections of `python-webrtc/cpp/NATIVE.md` and in `webrtc/utils/lifetime.py`.

pages.title: Build and release
pages.purpose: Building from sources with scikit-build-core and CMake, the prebuilt libwebrtc downloaded by `cmake/libwebrtc.cmake`, wheels built with cibuildwheel, and the steps in CONTRIBUTING.md.

pages.title: Testing
pages.purpose: The pytest suite in `tests`, the web-platform-tests in `tests/wpt`, the WebIDL comparison in `tests/idl`, fuzzing in `tests/fuzz`, and the sanitizer and clang-tidy scripts in `.github/scripts`.

pages.title: Benchmarks
pages.purpose: The benchmark suites and drivers in `benchmarks`, their method and caveats from benchmarks/README.md, and the results in benchmarks/RESULTS.md.

pages.title: Examples
pages.purpose: The runnable programs in `examples`: the echo peer, the recorder, the Janus live stream in the terminal and the voice chat with OpenAI.
